senses.sense_definition: A sudden outburst of violent activity or overwhelming emotion.

examples.text: Upon hearing the tragic news, she was overtaken by a violent <w>paroxysm</w> of weeping.
The dictator erupted in a furious <w>paroxysm</w> of rage when his orders were disobeyed.

senses.sense_definition: A sudden attack or violent worsening of a disease symptom, such as a severe coughing fit or seizure.

examples.text: A sudden <w>paroxysm</w> of coughing forced the speaker to stop and drink some water.
The patient suffered another painful <w>paroxysm</w> during the coldest hours of the night.

senses.sense_definition: A violent, sudden occurrence of a natural phenomenon, especially the most explosive phase of a volcanic eruption.

examples.text: The volcano produced an explosive <w>paroxysm</w> that sent ash high into the atmosphere.
Instruments recorded the sudden geological <w>paroxysm</w> long before the surface began to tremble.

senses.sense_definition: A sudden outburst of intense disagreement or political turmoil.

examples.text: The disputed election result plunged the entire nation into a political <w>paroxysm</w>.
A brief <w>paroxysm</w> of debate divided the council before a compromise could be reached.

senses.sense_definition: A sudden and disastrous upheaval or transformative change.

examples.text: Early geologists theorized that the landscape was formed by periodic <w>paroxysm</w> rather than slow erosion.
The sudden economic <w>paroxysm</w> dismantled industries that had flourished for decades.
